tagline: Down Cayuga Lake's east shore and off into farm country.
intro: Out of Montezuma, NY 90 crosses over the Thruway, the one place in the state where two highways of the same number cross, with no way from one onto the other. South of US 20 it keeps to the eastern shore of Cayuga Lake through Cayuga, Union Springs and Aurora. At King Ferry it turns east, away from the water, and runs through the farms of Genoa, Locke and Summerhill to Homer.

Its oldest ancestor is a stretch of the Great Western Turnpike, chartered in 1814 from Homer to Cayuga Lake, where ferries carried travelers across. The road also leads to historic homes, among them the last home of Harriet Tubman.

moments.title: Union Springs
moments.text: Offshore lies Frontenac Island, ceremonially important to the Cayuga and the only natural island in the Finger Lakes, though in 1859 nearly a third of it went into a railroad embankment.

moments.title: Aurora
moments.text: The lakeside village was a college town from 1868, when Henry Wells founded Wells College for women, until the college closed in 2024.
